28. It is now settled law that driving a vehicle by a victim without a driving licence, ipso facto does not lead to the conclusion of contributory negligence or that victim was not able to drive such vehicle properly, unless there are evidence on record in a particular case in this regard.
In the present case no such factual evidence placed on record by the insurance company.

Thus, driving a vehicle without a driving licence is an offence punishable under Section of MV Act but same cannot be ground to lead to the conclusion that there is contributory negligence on the part of victim.
Thus, on the facts of present case, it is held that there is no contributory negligence on the part of deceased.
